diagnosis: kernel_check_invariants aborted with 'unit large clause escaped propagation' — a large clause left unit (one non-false literal, still unassigned) at a claimed propagation fixpoint. Third member of the escaped-unit family after corpus 004 (decide-on-unpropagated-trail) and 005 (chronological-backjump mis-leveling), but a DIFFERENT cause: a lost learned-clause handoff, not a mis-leveled literal. Pinned with a per-step rule trace (every-step kernel_check_invariants + the rule applied); the window between the last CLEAN fixpoint and the abort was: Decide -> Reduce -> Propagate(conflict) -> Analyze -> Reduce -> Propagate -> Analyze -> Reduce -> Backjump -> Propagate(fixpoint) -> ABORT. The tell is ANALYZE RUNNING TWICE with no Backjump between. Root cause: propagate_guard did not require !k.pending.valid. After Analyze hands Backjump a learned clause (pending.valid = true, conflict_valid = false), the trail can still carry an unpropagated suffix, so Propagate's guard held and it ran — and found a SECOND conflict. That reaches the state (conflict_valid && pending.valid), in which Backjump is blocked (its guard needs !conflict_valid, so it never leaves Analyze a stale conflict) and ANALYZE IS THE ONLY APPLICABLE HANDOFF RULE. Analyze then OVERWRITES k.pending with the second conflict's clause. The first learned clause is thereby ORPHANED: it was already allocated in the arena, watched on two literals, and emitted to the proof, but its asserting literal is never assigned and Backjump never sees it. Because propagation is watch-driven — a clause is only revisited when one of its watched literals becomes false — nothing ever propagates it. Its non-asserting literals are all false at levels <= jump_level, so it survives the subsequent Backjump as a UNIT clause that no rule will ever look at: an escaped unit at the next fixpoint. NOTE this is NOT Backjump's stale-pending path (backjump.cpp), which is sound: that path's staleness test (asserting assigned, or any other literal non-false) holds EXACTLY when the pending clause is no longer unit, so discarding the assertion there is safe and normal propagation genuinely does take over. The overwrite path has no such check because the clause is dropped by Analyze, never reaching Backjump at all. Never reachable in DefaultPolicy, which consumes every pending clause with Backjump before propagating again (Propagate -> Analyze -> Backjump -> Propagate). Reachable only under a free N1 schedule, where Propagate is legal at that state. Fixed 2026-07-17 (plan decision (7525d52)): propagate_guard requires !k.pending.valid, making the (conflict_valid && pending.valid) state UNREACHABLE rather than merely unpleasant. Backjump is always applicable in its place (pending.valid && !conflict_valid), so no legal schedule loses progress and N1 is intact. The general invariant, the handoff analog of commit ae47ebf's propagation-fixpoint precondition: A RULE HANDOFF MUST BE CONSUMED BEFORE THE STATE IT DESCRIBES IS ADVANCED — a recorded conflict must be analyzed before tau changes (backjump_guard), and a pending learned clause must be backjumped before propagation resumes (propagate_guard).
